why: This is a stack where every entry also remembers the minimum of everything at or below it. Because a stack only changes at the top, that saved minimum stays valid until the entry is popped, which gives O(1) getMin.
hints: When you pop, the minimum might change. What information would let you know the new minimum right away?
Store pairs (value, min so far) on the stack. The min-so-far of a new entry is min(value, min-so-far of the entry below).
Push the pair, pop the pair, top = pair[0], getMin = pair[1]. Every operation is O(1); space O(n).
pitfalls: Duplicate minimums: popping one copy of 4 must keep 4 as the minimum if another copy remains, which per-entry minimums handle automatically.
Only top and getMin produce output; push and pop add nothing.
